_about: Multi-speaker story scenes (Oct 21 story-content brief). Read by StoryScenes (core/data/story_scenes.gd), played by StoryScenePlayer. Each step: [speaker, line, line...]; speaker = an NPC id (portrait + plate), NPC-PLAYER for the Wanderer, "" for narration, or "@set" followed by flags to set at that point. once_flag: skipped once set, set when played. sets: more flags set when played. Voice: docs/design/voice_bible.md.

steps: Someone has built a barricade out of weight plates painted regulation red. Behind it, a ferret in a pinstriped suit is timing a guard's push-ups with a silver stopwatch.
NPC-QUOTA
Forty-one, forty-two, and stop. Eleven percent slower than yesterday, which we will discuss at your review.
As for you, you entered at a walking pace of seven out of ten. That is disappointing, but it is at least measurable, which is more than I can say for most visitors.
NPC-PLAYER
You're the first person in this place who hasn't shouted at me. Who are you?
NPC-QUOTA
I am Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency. I designed the wheels, the schedules and the prison downstairs. The Chancellor does the shouting, and I do the arithmetic.
Hold still, please, while I measure you. Your grip is low and your stride is uneven. Your resolve, however, is unusually high, and that is an inefficiency I intend to remove.
NPC-QUOTA
Ninety-four seconds. You defeated me in ninety-four seconds, and I had allowed three hundred for the reverse.
I shall note it, as I note everything. That is not a compliment. I simply cannot leave a figure unsaid, and the Chancellor is not going to enjoy this one.
She clicks the stopwatch, steps through a side door marked for staff only, and is gone before the guard finishes his push-up.
On the arm of the Throne of Gains someone has left a schedule, timed to the second, and a silver stopwatch, still running.
NPC-FLEX
Quota's gone. She was off to the Capital before the dust had even settled; she always did like to leave early.
We'll keep her schedule, because it will make good kindling. And breathe, son. Nobody in this house is on the clock any more.
By the last energy wheel, a ferret in pinstripes stands over Rollo's crews with a stopwatch. They are lying in the sun, and she is still timing them.
NPC-QUOTA
You. Again. You cost me the Gainlands in four hours and twelve minutes. I have had the figure framed.
These wheels lit the facade at a hundred and ten percent. Now they are 'resting'. Do you know what rest is? Unmeasured time.
NPC-PLAYER
They're allowed to stop.
NPC-QUOTA
Nobody is allowed anything. People are scheduled. Let me schedule you.
NPC-QUOTA
Eighty-one seconds. Faster than last time. You have improved by fourteen percent.
That was not a compliment. I simply cannot leave a figure unsaid.
NPC-ROLLO
The crews voted... while you two were busy. You're staying put... till Flex's people come down. Some of those wheels... had children on them. They'd like a word.
NPC-QUOTA
Detained. I have never been detained. I do not even know how long it takes.
I will find out. I will time every minute of it.
Two of Rollo's crew take her by the elbows, gently, the way you'd lift something off a high shelf. Somewhere near the gate, for the first time in ten years, she stops clicking the stopwatch.
The Prototype Bay smells of hot iron and burnt sugar. A war machine squats on a pallet: half oven, half cannon, one wheel still in its packing straw.
NPC-CRUMB
ATTEN-TION! Inspection! Who put a dent in my souffle cannon? Battle stations, all of you! This is not a drill, it is a souffle, and it will rise on schedule!
NPC-CRUMB
And what is THIS? A civilian, wandering about my bay unsupervised, with flavour on his breath! You are out of uniform and out of bounds, soldier, and I call it a disgrace.
Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense, and you will stand up straight when you hear it. Taste is a weakness, soldier. Paste is a strategy.
NPC-CRUMB
Whisk formation! Field-test the prototype on the intruder while I attend a ration meeting. I want a full report, and I want it bland.
He salutes the machine, the machine salutes back with a ladle, and the Colonel marches out before it has finished preheating.
The war machine sags and steams. Taped to its side is an inspection card under a seal of crossed forks: PASSED. NEEDS MORE SALT. - COL. C. CRUMB.
NPC-BASIL
Um. The Colonel's gone. He cleared out his whole office overnight, and he took the paste recipe with him, though I can't think why he'd need to.
I've seen that recipe, you see, and it's only one word long, and the word is 'paste'.
NPC-ESCOFFINA
He left before dessert, the way he always did. They say he's feeding the whole Capital now, out of a factory.
Grey food out of a tap, for a whole city. Somebody ought to sit that man down at a table and teach him what cooking is for.
At the end of the Vat Floor, behind a door with a ration hatch, is a real kitchen: copper pans, a cold stove, and a badger in a medal-covered chef's coat guarding a locked pantry.
NPC-CRUMB
ATTENTION! You are standing in a restricted pantry, soldier! Every recipe on those shelves has been confiscated for the war effort!
Which war? The war on FLAVOUR, son! Every citizen fed the same ration, at the same minute, from the same tap, and not one complaint about the seasoning.
NPC-PLAYER
Marlo says you can't taste it either. Is that why everyone else has to eat it?
NPC-CRUMB
Taste is a weakness, soldier, and I have none! Golems, whisk formation, to the vats! Nobody touches my pantry!
NPC-CRUMB
Stand down. Stand DOWN. I said... oh, everyone's already lying down. Very well.
The pantry door swings open on shelves of confiscated jars: pickles, jams, and a wheel of cheese with a ration number stamped on it. Out on the floor, a vat coughs and stops.
NPC-CRUMB
I invented the paste because nobody could get it wrong, soldier. You can't burn it, you can't oversalt it, and you can't spoil a regiment's dinner with it.
And you can't... taste it. I haven't tasted anything in years, you know. I thought if nobody could, nobody would notice that I couldn't.
NPC-MARLO
Then you'll learn again. The Grand Chef is taking students, and she starts every one of them the same way: first, water.
NPC-CRUMB
...Yes, Chef.
Roots as thick as a cart grip the mill wheel. Someone has trimmed them, very neatly, into the shape of a smiling man in a circlet.
NPC-CLIPWELL
Do mind the topiary, if you would. That's His Perfection, seen from the left. The right side is still filling in.
NPC-CLIPWELL
Hortensia Clipwell, Royal Groundskeeper. I am the one who outlawed composting. All that rot lying about in heaps, being honest with everybody. So untidy.
NPC-PLAYER
Nothing rots down here any more, and the whole place feels wrong for it.
NPC-CLIPWELL
Isn't it lovely? I brought the Archdruid a little seed as a gift: life that never ends. She was so very sad, you see, and now nothing ever has to go.
And now, I'm afraid, I have a weed to remove.
NPC-CLIPWELL
Well. You've made a dreadful mess of my hedges, and I shall be sending a note.
She opens a wide green umbrella, steps neatly over the roots and walks away up the ravine toward the Capital road, not one hair out of place.
NPC-BRAMBLE
The Groundskeeper's gone. She packed her shears and left for the Capital the very moment the Archdruid woke.
NPC-BRAMBLE
She left one pair behind in a compost heap, and Granny Gristle has kept them. 'Found, not stolen,' she told me, twice, before I'd even asked.
Beside the Sick Patch, a hare in groundskeeper green is measuring Old Fern's seedling with a ruler. It is an inch over regulation, and she has written that down.
NPC-CLIPWELL
Out of regulation. Everything is out of regulation now, the lawns and the hedges both. They grow in whatever direction they please.
NPC-FERN
That's what hedges DO.
NPC-CLIPWELL
I gave her the seed because she was crying. I thought, if nothing ever ends, then nobody ever has to cry again.
That's tidy, isn't it? Isn't that tidy?
NPC-PLAYER
Nothing grew there for ten years.
NPC-FERN
Granny Gristle needs hands on the compost rows down in the Dump, sorting peel from shell all day long. It's messy work, and you'd hate it. Good. It's yours if you want it.
NPC-CLIPWELL
...No. I will not be forgiven by a compost heap. I shall find somewhere that still keeps its hedges at a proper height.
She walks away down the exact middle of the path. She does not look back at the seedling, and it goes on growing without her permission.
A peacock in a lavender coat sweeps across the lobby with a ribbon, a pair of golden scissors and a speaking trumpet.
NPC-PLUME
Great news, citizens! The D.N.A. has been freed, a change His Perfection fully supports and in fact arranged!
And you must be the volunteer. A Certificate of Participation. Frame it, or don't. It's been notarized either way.
NPC-AGNES
That's Percival Plume, dear. Deputy Minister of Good News. He drafted the transfer. Every page of it.
NPC-PLUME
And had a clerk file it, on a Tuesday, I believe! Must dash. Ribbons to cut, a Capital to reassure. Toodle-oo!
He snips the ribbon, which was holding nothing up, and is gone before Agnes can find the right form.
The castle gate is white and gold and perfectly symmetrical. In its shadow, with her hood up, stands the woman who pulled you out of the woods, as though she was always going to be here.
NPC-ELOWEN
Don't look so surprised. I told you somebody had to watch the door while you knocked it down.
NPC-PLUME
Great news, citizens! The traitor has been located! Please hold your applause until she has been removed.
Guards in polished armour pour from the gatehouse, and they are not coming for you. They are coming for her.
NPC-PLUME
Miss {rescuer_full}, I presume! Former junior Path-ologist, absent without leave, who removed one item of laboratory property that has been walking about ever since.
@set
rescuer_named
NPC-PLUME
Now don't fret, Miss Vey. Your father is ever so understanding about these things. Take her home, gentlemen, and do take the long way round.
NPC-ELOWEN
Don't follow me, {wanderer}! Get to the top of that castle. It's the only way any of this ends.
They are through a side door before you can reach it, and on this side the door has no handle at all.
NPC-PLAYER
{rescuer}. Her name is {rescuer}. I asked her twice, and both times she said 'a friend', and both times I let her leave it at that.
The Necrocrat wing's archive is paper from floor to ceiling. On the desk, under a paperweight shaped like a peacock, lies a memo, the ink still wet.
MEMO. To: His Perfection. From: P. Plume. Re: the leak in the lab. The junior Path-ologist has been returned to the Path-ology Lab beneath the forest, to her father. Handled. Promotion?
NPC-PLUME
Ah! You found my memo. Isn't it well written? I used the active voice.
Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News. I drafted the transfer of the D.N.A., notarized it, had a clerk file it, and read it out on every loudspeaker in the land.
NPC-PLAYER
Where is this Lab? Where did you take her?
NPC-PLUME
Beneath the forest where you... oh, I shouldn't have said that. Never mind. Great news: your visit is being declined!
NPC-PLUME
This is a setback. A temporary, fully reversible, not-at-all-my-fault setback.
I'll draft a statement. 'Minister Plume bravely withdrew.' Yes. Bravely.
He withdraws, bravely, at a run. You fold the memo into your pocket, and two phrases go with it: beneath the forest, and her father.
NPC-ELDER
Sit down, dearie. Word came from the Capital this morning, and you aren't going to like it.
NPC-ELDER
Plume's men took a girl at the castle gate, the same one who carried you out of those woods. {rescuer_full}, they called her.
I knew whose daughter she was the day she sent you through my cave. Her father worked in my laboratory once, and I held that against her for far too long. I was wrong to do it.
NPC-ELDER
I've been wrong about people before, and I swore to myself that I never would be again. It seems I've gone and done it twice.
NPC-PLAYER
Where did they take her?
NPC-ELDER
Back where she came from, I expect: somewhere with glass walls and no windows. That's one door I can't open for you, dearie. Not yet.
Eat something. You'll want your strength for the day it does open.
NPC-WREN
We saw them take her at the gate: four guards, and a peacock with a speaking trumpet. We couldn't get anywhere near her.
NPC-WREN
The Wrinkles are watching every door out of that castle. If they move her again, we will know.
Her name goes into the true record, whatever else happens. I can promise you that much.
The hatch opens on white light and a smell of disinfectant. A staircase of clean steel goes down through the roots of the forest where you woke up.
Everything about this place is familiar in the way a bruise is familiar. Your hands are shaking. You go down anyway.
A white room, three paces by four. Ten years of tally marks on the wall in rows of five, scratched with a spoon handle. Low down, where a child could reach, a drawing in four colors.
Someone is sitting under the drawing with her knees up and her hands bound, as if she has been keeping it company.
NPC-ELOWEN
Took you long enough, Tess.
NPC-PLAYER
Tess?
NPC-ELOWEN
That's what I called you, when we were small and you were too important to be called anything shorter.
They put me in your cell. My father calls it educational, and the worst of it is that he means it.
NPC-ELOWEN
I'll walk behind you. I know every door down here, and which ones scream.
NPC-ELOWEN
Whatever he says in there, he'll say it kindly. That's the worst part. Don't listen to the voice, Tess. Watch the hands.
This is the only room in the Lab with a rug. On the desk lies a journal in a neat, slanted hand, and its last entry is ten years old.
"The Minister knelt to the King. I was asked to hold the east door. I held it open. The boy will be safer with us than with sentiment. We will learn so much." - A. Siphon
NPC-ELOWEN
That's his handwriting.
He told me the King died of a fever. He told me you were a patient, so I brought you soup.
NPC-PLAYER
{rescuer}...
NPC-ELOWEN
Don't. Not yet. If you're kind to me now, I won't be able to walk in there.
This is the only room in the Lab with a rug. On the desk lies a journal in a neat, slanted hand beside a child's drawing: 'For Papa, from {rescuer}.' The last entry is ten years old.
"The Minister knelt to the King. I was asked to hold the east door. I held it open. The boy will be safer with us than with sentiment. We will learn so much." - A. Siphon
NPC-PLAYER
Siphon is {rescuer}'s father, and he held the door for them.
The Extraction Theater: tiered seats of white steel around a single chair. Dr. Ambrose Siphon looks up from a bench of humming glass, neat, polite and not at all surprised.
NPC-SIPHON
Subject 1, and my daughter too! Both of you home at once. I shall have to rearrange the whole schedule.
Remarkable. You've grown at least two inches, and the time away has done wonders for your posture. I'll want measurements.
NPC-ELOWEN
You held the door, Dad, the night they killed the King and Queen. I read it in your own hand.
NPC-SIPHON
I held a door, sweetheart. Doors are held every day. What came through it was the Minister's choice, not mine.
NPC-ELOWEN
You told me he was a patient, and I brought him soup for years.
NPC-SIPHON
And it was very good soup. You were always confused about kindness. It made you a poor scientist and a lovely daughter.
Please, both of you, sit. This will only drain a little.
NPC-ELOWEN
Tess. His Protocols run on switches, and I know where every one is. I'll take one down each turn. You do the rest.
The Extraction Theater: tiered seats of white steel around a single chair. Dr. Ambrose Siphon looks up from a bench of humming glass, neat, polite and not at all surprised.
NPC-SIPHON
Subject 1, you came back to us! And you've grown. Remarkable, after so many cycles; I'll want measurements.
NPC-SIPHON
My daughter is resting in your old room. She is confused, poor thing. She thinks she rescued something.
Assistants always come home, and so do subjects, it seems. Please, sit. This will only drain a little.
The tanks go dark one by one. Siphon sits down among the cables on the floor of his own theater, like a man who has dropped something very small.
NPC-SIPHON
You were never a Subject. Maren said so, and I called it sentiment.
I called a great many things sentiment.
NPC-ELOWEN
Get up, Dad. You're going to {town}. Agnes has a form for you, Maren has a great deal to say, and you are going to listen to all of it.
NPC-SIPHON
...Yes. Yes, I suppose I am.
The four colors rise out of the tanks, through the roof and into the forest, where the trees lean toward them like flowers. You do not feel stronger. You feel less alone.
NPC-ELOWEN
My name is {rescuer_full}. Vey was my mother's. I wanted to say it to you properly once, somewhere with a roof.
The tanks go dark one by one. Siphon sits down among the cables on the floor of his own theater, like a man who has dropped something very small.
Footsteps in the corridor behind you, quick and uneven. Somebody has picked the lock of Cell 4 from the inside.
NPC-ELOWEN
Took you long enough, Tess. I got tired of waiting and let myself out.
NPC-ELOWEN
You held the door, Dad, the night they killed the King and Queen. It's in your journal, in your own hand.
NPC-SIPHON
I held a door, sweetheart. What came through it was the Minister's choice.
NPC-ELOWEN
No. It was yours too. Get up. You're going to {town}, and you're going to listen to every word Maren says.
NPC-SIPHON
...Yes. I suppose I am.
The four colors rise out of the tanks, through the roof and into the forest, where the trees lean toward them like flowers. You do not feel stronger. You feel less alone.
NPC-ELOWEN
My name is {rescuer_full}. Vey was my mother's. I wanted to say it to you properly once, somewhere with a roof.
Someone is sitting on a rock at the mouth of the Forgotten Cave with her hood up, sharpening a pencil with a scalpel.
NPC-ELOWEN
You freed a whole Path on your own, with a deck you've had for about a week. I didn't think I would be saying that so soon.
Let me see your hands. They're steadier than they were, and that's good. It's the first thing I've been able to cross off my list in a long time.
NPC-PLAYER
Who are you?
NPC-ELOWEN
A friend. That's still all I can tell you, and I'm sorry that it isn't more.
I won't come into town, though. The old woman with the shell looks at me as if I owe her something, and she's probably right.
NPC-ELOWEN
Keep going. I'll know when the next one falls, because the woods go quiet for a moment whenever a Path comes loose.
The hooded figure is back at the cave mouth, this time with two cups of something hot. She hands you one without asking whether you want it.
NPC-ELOWEN
Two Paths free. I could hear the town singing from all the way out here. It was terrible singing, but they were singing.
NPC-PLAYER
You knew I'd come back here.
NPC-ELOWEN
You always did come back to the same places. Even when you were...
Drink your tea. It's for the shaking.
NPC-PLAYER
Even when I was what?
NPC-ELOWEN
Even when you were somewhere they wouldn't let you leave. Ask me something easier, please.
NPC-PLAYER
All right. What's your favourite colour?
NPC-ELOWEN
I have four of them. Next question.
She is waiting at the cave mouth again, and this time her hood is down, as though she has forgotten to put it up. Her eyes are tired and very sure.
NPC-ELOWEN
Three. At first I told myself you only reminded me of someone, a friend I lost when we were both children. Now I'm starting to think...
No. Not until I'm certain. Too many people round here say things before they're sure of them, and I won't be another.
NPC-PLAYER
Everywhere I go, someone tells me a story about a little prince, and then they look at me and stop talking. You knew me before all this, didn't you?
NPC-ELOWEN
I knew a boy who fell on his behind trying to lift a dumbbell twice his size, and who ate the frosting off every layer of his birthday cake.
You'd have liked him. He was hopeless at hiding anything.
The cave mouth is quiet. This time she is on her feet with her cloak fastened and a satchel of four-coloured vials over one shoulder, ready to go somewhere.
NPC-ELOWEN
All four. Can you hear it? The kingdom is breathing again. It's like voices through a wall, except that now the wall is coming down.
There's only the Capital left now. There's only him.
NPC-PLAYER
Come with me.
NPC-ELOWEN
I'll be at the castle gate when you get there. Somebody has to watch the door while you knock it down.
And when it's over, I'll tell you all of it. My name first. I promise.
A gravedigger in a battered top hat leans on his shovel among the headstones, consulting a little black book.
NPC-HOB
Evening! Old Hob, at your service. I dig, mostly, though there's not been a lot of call for it these ten years. Nobody's been collected, you see, on account of the paperwork. Heh.
NPC-PLAYER
What are you writing?
NPC-HOB
Appointments. Let's have a look for you, shall we... hm. Not for a good long while yet. Lovely! That's what I like to see.
NPC-HOB
Mind the cairn at the end of the row, though. Something under it is still counting its turns, and it's rude to keep a thing like that waiting. Heh.
NPC-HOB
Still digging, and taking it slowly. Two particular graves I've been at, these ten years now. I like to take my time over the important ones. Heh.
NPC-PLAYER
What are you writing?
NPC-HOB
Appointments. Let's have a look for you, shall we... hm. Not for a good long while yet. Lovely! That's what I like to see.
NPC-HOB
The intake's open again, did you hear? Busy week. Gerald's number finally came up, lovely chap, and he asked if he could stay on for one more pot first. I said yes. There's no rush, in my line.
NPC-HOB
Agnes stayed on, of course. Somebody has to put the forms right, so I've pencilled her in for later. Much later. Heh.
NPC-HOB
Ah. You did it, then, the castle and all.
Then I've two graves to finish properly, up in Grave Row in the city. Come by when you're ready. No rush; there never is, with me.
NPC-HOB
Back again! Walked them all the way home, I did. Lovely evening for it.
NPC-PLAYER
What are you writing?
NPC-HOB
Appointments. Let's see now... you're not down for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.
NPC-HOB
Hm? You? Not on my list. Off you pop. Heh.
I'd charge you a handling fee for the trouble, only you've nothing on you that I want. Heh.
An old gravedigger is pacing out a hole beside the weight racks, counting under his breath.
NPC-HOB
Just measuring, don't mind me. Lovely broad shoulders you all have up here, so it'll be nice roomy work when it comes. Not that any of it's come lately, mind. Heh.
NPC-PLAYER
What are you writing?
NPC-HOB
Appointments. Let's have a look for you, shall we... hm. Not for a good long while yet. Lovely! You carry on, then, and mind your back around all this lifting. Heh.
NPC-HOB
Lovely building, this. Can't collect a single soul in it, mind, because the paperwork won't let me past the lobby, so I've been sat here with my flask ever since the transfer.
They gave me a number and all, same as everybody. Makes a nice change, that, seeing as I'm usually the one who calls them. Heh.
NPC-PLAYER
What are you writing?
NPC-HOB
Appointments, same as ever. Now let's see, you're... hm. No, you're not down for a good long while yet. Lovely! That's what I like to see.
NPC-HOB
Intake's moving again, and Agnes waved me straight through with a smile. First time in ten years nobody's asked me for Form 27-B, mind, and the appointment book's filling up nicely. Heh.
NPC-HOB
Just measuring. Mind you, the Chef's soups add years to people, which is bad for business and good for everybody else. Heh.
NPC-PLAYER
What are you writing?
NPC-HOB
Oh, only appointments. Let's see now... no, you're not down for a good long while yet, and that's just what I like to see. Lovely! Heh.
NPC-HOB
Nothing's died in this valley in ten years, not so much as a beetle or a leaf. Unnatural, that.
Gives a fellow a lot of free time. I've taken up knitting. Heh.
NPC-HOB
Hear that? Things rotting properly again. Lovely sound, that - it means something's about to grow.
NPC-HOB
Just measuring. There's a lot of very tidy people in this city, and tidy is easy to measure.
NPC-PLAYER
And the man in the castle?
NPC-HOB
Him? Hm.
Pencilled in. Heh.
NPC-HOB
Just measuring. Ran into a peacock earlier, all trumpet and ribbons.
Oh, I've got HIM in pen. Heh. Not soon, mind. I just wanted it to last.
Someone is walking down the imperial road in faded pastel regulation clothes, a bedroll over one shoulder. Brannoch has stopped writing in his notebook.
NPC-ISLA
Hi, Dad. I know. I should have written.
NPC-GATEKEEPER
Hm.
NPC-GATEKEEPER
Eight years. Kept the gate open every night, in case.
NPC-ISLA
They had us painting the same front door for eight years. Every time I asked to leave, the form came back "pending".
NPC-GATEKEEPER
...You've got your mother's curls. Still can't keep a ribbon in them.
NPC-ISLA
And your nose. Mum always said that was the unlucky part.
NPC-GATEKEEPER
Wrote you in the book. Every day. "Isla. Not yet."
Today it says "home".
NPC-ISLA
You're the one who knocked the castle over? That 'Hm' was Dad saying thank you. Thank you from me, too.
NPC-ISLA
I keep walking to the gate and back. Nobody stops me. I keep expecting somebody to stop me.
Dad oiled the hinges this morning. It doesn't even lock. He just likes the sound of it opening now.
Grave Row, at dusk. At the end of the identical rows stand two new headstones, and they are not identical. Someone has carved them by hand: a crown, a harp, four colours in a ring.
Half the city has come, and nobody told them to. Wren holds the true record; Maren holds a pie she has forgotten she is carrying.
NPC-HOB
Ten years I've been digging these two. Slowly. I didn't want to finish before they could be visited properly.
NPC-AGNES
Two forms, filed ten years ago, stamped by me. And a third, for a little boy, that I never had the heart to file.
I'm tearing that one up now, dear. With great pleasure.
NPC-ELDER
He used to say the Paths argued like family. She used to say that was the point.
A warm wind comes up the row, out of season. Two figures stand by the headstones, the way people stand in a doorway when they are leaving and not sorry to.
NPC-KING
Look at you. You came home.
NPC-QUEEN
Carry them gently, love. All four of them.
She hums the first bars of the lullaby, and does not need to finish it. You know the rest.
NPC-HOB
Right then, Your Majesties. Mind the step. It's a long one, but it's downhill all the way.
NPC-HOB
And you, Agnes. I've had you down for this a very long time.
NPC-AGNES
One more week, Hob. Prudence needs a proper handover, and somebody has to explain the new handbook to Mortimer.
NPC-HOB
Hm. Pencilled in. Heh.
When you look again there are two headstones, a top hat bobbing away down the row, and a great deal of warm wind.
NPC-GATEKEEPER
Hm. She's home.
Notebook's full of her name, so I've started a new one. First page says yours. Spelled it right, this time.
